content.title: About
content.content: The pork, rice and cheese burrito is a Mexican dish consisting of a large wheat tortilla wrapped around a filling of tender pork, seasoned rice and melted cheese. It provides a balanced mix of protein, carbohydrates and fats for sustained energy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Burritos originated in northern Mexico where wheat flour is more common than corn.
Pork is often marinated in chipotle, coriander and lime, giving it a smoky flavor.
Mexican rice is typically cooked with tomato sauce and turmeric, which adds color and taste.
The cheese used is usually a blend of cheddar and Mexican “queso” that melts smoothly.
Burritos are commonly served with salsa, guacamole and sour cream, allowing diners to adjust spiciness and creaminess.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Pork supplies high‑quality protein essential for muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Energy‑rich carbohydrates
items.content: Rice provides complex carbs that release energy slowly, helping you feel full longer.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Cheese contributes calcium and phosphorus, important for bone health.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Both pork and rice contain B1, B3 and B6 vitamins that support metabolic processes.

items.title: Dietary fiber (if whole‑grain rice is used)
items.content: Whole‑grain rice adds fiber, aiding digestion and blood‑sugar control.

items.title: High fat content
items.content: The cheese and pork can make the burrito calorie‑dense; watch portion sizes if weight management is a goal.

items.title: Sodium levels
items.content: Salt used in the pork rub and cheese can increase sodium intake, which may be a concern for hypertension.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Cheese may trigger allergic reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk protein allergy.

items.title: Digestive heaviness
items.content: A rich meat and cheese filling can be heavy for those with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Burritos are hand‑held; cut them in half for easier handling. Warm them in a microwave or skillet until the cheese melts. Top with fresh salsa, guacamole or sour cream to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared burritos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For longer storage, wrap tightly in plastic and freeze for up to 2 months. Reheat to an internal temperature of 75 °C before eating.
